ops.after_html: Alabama mineral ownership tracks the county courthouse, not a state map. Start with the county or city that holds the deed, lease, and division order for the tract.

The Alabama record differs by how the interest arrived, inherited, divided among family, tied to an unsolicited offer, or sitting on leased-but-undrilled acreage, and each path points to a different first document to pull.

Mineral rights, royalty interests, overriding royalties, non-participating royalties, and working interests carry different powers and different exposure under an Alabama lease. The acquisition file names the interest before it prices it.
Alabama production runs through the Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane fairway and the south Alabama oil trend, and each carries its own decline pattern, operator history, and paid-decimal reality.
Deeds, probate records, division orders, and a proposed conveyance answer different parts of an Alabama mineral sale. These guides walk through what each document needs to say.

Buyers who value an Alabama mineral position for its own cash flow ask different questions than an owner comparing a single lump-sum offer, and the difference shows up in how the interest gets modeled.

Rolling Alabama mineral or royalty proceeds into a like-kind replacement runs on the same 45-day identification and 180-day closing clock as any other 1031 exchange, with rules specific to mineral and royalty interests.
